text: The year was 1889, and the last natural forest on Earth was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Eli, a young botanist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the industrial metropolis encroaching upon the natural world. The city, Paris, was preparing to unveil the Eiffel Tower, a towering symbol of iron and ambition that loomed over the landscape, casting a long shadow over the remaining green spaces.
